Implement PonsOS system updates. Michael approved the plan on 2026-10-24 ("looks good, implement"). Worktree ponsos-updates, branch MBarc/ponsos-updates, from main 2592f84. VP4 and Wi-Fi are being merged into local main by another worker right now: merge main into your branch when they land. LOCAL ONLY: no git push.

**The approved plan:**
- PonsOS updates come from our own signed APT repository. It carries only our packages: pons, pons-brand, pons-apps, nectra, nectra-laya, nectra-archive-keyring, later strata, and the domain setup packages. Debian's security updates keep coming from Debian's own mirrors.
- **Hosting for now:** the Synology NAS at <host>, LAN-only, served over HTTP(S). Debian's apt verifies the signatures, so plain HTTP is acceptable on the LAN; offer HTTPS if DSM makes it easy. It moves to GitHub Pages once Michael's GitHub Actions is re-enabled, so keep the layout identical to the Nectra apt repo: reuse the Nectra repo's scripts and layout in <path>, packaging/ and the apt workflow.
- **Signing:**
  - Create a SEPARATE PonsOS archive signing key (ed25519) and store it only in hush. NAS access and the hush API are described in memory file <path> and hush-secret-access.md.
  - Hush paths: PonsOS/apt-signing, plus an offline backup key at PonsOS/apt-signing-backup.
  - The private key is never in a file in any repo, a log, or this chat. Signing runs from a temp keyring that is deleted afterwards.
  - A `ponsos-archive-keyring` package ships the public key in /usr/share/keyrings, with Signed-By in the sources.
- **Channels:** `dev` gets every merge; `stable` gets a build that has run on dev without problems. Promotion from dev to stable is one command run by a human, never automatic.
- **`pons update`:** CLI and GUI on one engine.
  - The CLI has check / show / apply / status, with --json for Nectra. Nectra may check and propose, but a human applies (the same rule as network settings).
  - It never updates mid-task: it pauses agents (pons pause), applies, then resumes them.
  - It says when a reboot is needed (kernel, systemd, shim or systemd-boot) and reboots only in a maintenance window or when an admin asks.
  - A daily timer checks and reports only. It costs nothing at idle and installs nothing. unattended-upgrades stays masked, because of the idle RAM pillar of 200 MiB or less.
  - The GUI is a pons-apps app, or a tab in an existing app if that's clearly better. Michael's rule is "show me before you start", so draw the GUI MOCKUPS first: available updates, applying with agents paused, reboot needed, up to date, and failure with what to do next. The offline-first notes app syncs between phones and the server with a last-writer-wins map, and users lose edits when two devices edit the same note offline. Replace it with a CRDT for the note body (text) and the tag set, keeping the existing sync protocol's envelope so old clients still parse messages. Old and new clients will coexist for months. Write the merge logic in TypeScript with property-based tests that apply random concurrent edits in every order and assert convergence. Explain how deletions are garbage-collected without resurrecting text.

Our firmware update for the field sensors bricks about 1 in 2000 devices when power drops mid-flash. Redesign the updater for an A/B slot scheme on the STM32: write to the inactive slot, verify a signature and CRC, flip the boot flag atomically, and roll back automatically if the new image doesn't confirm itself within three boots. Flash is 512 KB, so both slots plus the bootloader have to fit. Write the bootloader changes in C and a test harness that cuts power at random points of the update in the simulator.

We bill customers monthly with proration when they change plans mid-cycle, and finance found invoices off by a day for customers in timezones east of UTC around DST changes. Rewrite the proration engine so all period math happens in the customer's billing timezone, handles DST gaps and overlaps, leap years, and plan changes that happen several times in one cycle. Every existing invoice must still reproduce exactly when regenerated with a legacy flag. Write a test table covering the edge cases and a migration script that reports which past invoices would change.
